title: 第一章　培养有意识的公民

children: 1917年2月革命爆发时，德米特里·富尔曼诺夫（Dmitri Furmanov）正在家乡伊万诺沃担任教员，给工人们上夜校课。这座工业城市位于莫斯科东北部。这位25岁的兼职作家、曾在第一次世界大战初期退学离开莫斯科大学加入红十字会的学生，立即投身于蔓延的革命委员会和党小组网络。革命发生一个月后，他在日记中写道：“‘社会工作者’这一光荣头衔让我强大了十倍……它要求一个人尽可能地细致、理智和严厉，它灌输意识、个人判断和个人自我评价……在这一新学校中，原则被制定出来，意志得到淬炼，计划得以制定，行动方案也随之产生……这场伟大的革命在我身上也带来了一个心理转折点。”

When the revolution broke out in February 1917, Dmitri Furmanov was working as an instructor, teaching evening classes to workers in his industrial home town of Ivanovo, northeast of Moscow. A part-time writer and former student who had quit Moscow University to join the Red Cross in the initial weeks of World War I, the 25-year-old Furmanov immediately involved himself in the sprawling network of revolutionary councils and party cells. One month into the revolution he noted in his diary: “The honorable title ‘social worker’ has made me ten times more powerful . . . it obligates one to be as careful, sensible, and strict as possible, it inculcates consciousness, personal judgment, and personal self-evaluation . . . In this new school principles are worked out, the will is hardened, a plan is created, a course of action . . . This great revolution has brought about a psychological turning point in me as well.”

正如富尔曼诺夫所暗示的，革命作为一种新的、理性的、公正的社会秩序的预兆，按自身的形象改造了他。在进入他的个人生活时，革命意志使他的思想和身体运作合理化了。然而，并非富尔曼诺夫这一时期的所有日记条目都如此慷慨激昂。许多段落充满了自我怀疑和为自己政治定位的焦虑尝试：在1917年8月一篇题为“我是谁？”的条目中，他试图定义自己的政治立场：他是“社会革命党人、国际主义者，还是最高纲领派”？两年后——那时他已加入布尔什维克党，并在一支参加内战的红军师里担任要职，出任政治委员——他仍然抱怨自己训练不足且政治热情起伏不定，这表明他的心理生活并未与革命完全对齐。

富尔曼诺夫是众多认同俄罗斯民主知识分子并拥抱革命、将其视为新时代曙光的教师、作家、医生之一。对他们来说，这标志着由前几代知识分子描绘的社会和人类转型蓝图即将实施并变为现实的长期期待时刻。这些蓝图意味着人类可以彻底更新，具有无限可能，也能够臻于完美；社会主义“新人”的愿景凝聚了这些设想。马克西姆·高尔基在1917年4月的《新生活报》一篇文章中表达了这些期望：“政治生活的新结构要求我们拥有灵魂的新结构。”富尔曼诺夫以惊人直白的方式接受了这一指令。对他来说，建设一个新的、更好的社会的承诺，在很大程度上包含了更新自我的承诺。

As Furmanov suggested, the revolution as a harbinger of a new, rational, and just social order transformed him in its image. In entering his personal life, the revolutionary will rationalized the workings of his mind and body. Yet not all of Furmanov’s diary entries of this period were so exuberant in tone. Many passages resonated with self-doubt and anxious attempts to position himself politically: in an entry for August 1917 entitled “Who am I?” he sought to define his politics: was he “a socialist-revolutionary, an internationalist, a maximalist”? Two years later—by which time he had joined the Bolshevik party and assumed a responsible post as a political commissar in a Red division fighting in the Civil War—he still complained about his inadequate training and uneven political enthusiasm, indicating that his psychological life was not fully aligned with the revolution.

Furmanov was one of many teachers, writers, doctors who identified with Russia’s democratic intelligentsia and embraced the revolution as the dawn of a new age. For them it signified the long-anticipated moment when scenarios of social and human transformation, sketched out by preceding generations of the intelligentsia, were to be implemented and become reality. These scenarios suggested total re-newal, total possibility, and total perfectibility of humankind, and they were coined in the vision of the socialist “new man.” Maxim Gorky expressed these expectations in an article in his newspaper, New Life, in April 1917: “The new structure of political life demands from us a new structure of the soul.” Furmanov took on this imperative in strikingly literal fashion. For him the commitment to produce a new, better society, entailed in important measure a commitment to renew himself.

对在革命行动中表达出来的新的社会和个人生活形式的献身精神，团结了所有阵营的革命者，从1917年10月掌权的布尔什维克，到他们激烈的批评者马克西姆·高尔基，再到政治上摇摆不定的活动家德米特里·富尔曼诺夫。作为俄罗斯知识分子的成员，他们共同抱有一种道德承诺，即将生命献给共同事业、社会进步、人民福祉或历史的前进。知识分子的任务是教育和启蒙，将俄罗斯的“黑暗群众”提升到真正“人”（chelovek）和具有批判思维的“人格”（lichnost'）的高度，然后这些人会起来反抗压迫者，从而推动历史沿着其预定的解放轨迹前进。凭借其享有的优越教育，知识分子对历史规律有着卓越的洞察力。这种先锋角色赋予了他引导他人走向光明的权利，但也赋予了他一种道德义务，即在与历史的交融中，过一种高度投入而纯洁的生活——去体现那备受推崇的新人的品质。

The dedication to new forms of social and individual life, expressed in the act of revolution, united revolutionaries of all camps, from the Bolsheviks who took power in October 1917, to their fierce critic Maxim Gorky, to the politically wavering activist Dmitri Furmanov. As members of the Russian intelligentsia, they shared a moral commitment to devote their lives to a common cause, social progress, the well-being of the people, or the advancement of history. The task of the intelligentsia was to educate and enlighten, to raise Russia’s “dark masses” to the stature of true “human beings” (chelovek) and critically thinking “personalities” (lichnost’), who would then rise up against their oppressors and thus move history along on its preordained emancipatory trail. By dint of his privileged education, the intelligent had superior insight into the laws of history. This vanguard role gave him the right to direct others toward the light, but it also imparted a moral duty to live a life of exceptional devotion and purity, in communion with history—to embody the qualities of the vaunted new man.

这种关于新人的思想，源于19世纪作家和评论家尼古拉·车尔尼雪夫斯基的小说《怎么办？》。这部小说对“新人类”做了影响深远的描绘——这些年轻人以能够过完全理性的生活并全身心地投身于革命而著称。这些“新时代的人”每一个都是“坚强的人格”：“大胆、坚定、无情，能够掌握事物并紧紧抓住它们，不让它们从手指间滑落”。在遥远的某一天，这些革命者会变成日常类型，但在目前（1863年），他们是“稀有品种”：“他们就像茶里的茶碱，像美酒的香气；他们是其力量和芬芳。他们是最好的人群中的花朵，是能量的原始源泉，是盐中之盐！”

车尔尼雪夫斯基创作《怎么办？》是为了发出行动号召，而它也正是被如此接收的。沙俄晚期的大批激进学生按照书中的形象塑造自己；列宁称其为他一生中最重要的一本书；迟至1933年，被纳粹指控策划国会纵火案的共产国际领导人格奥尔基·季米特洛夫在柏林监狱等待审判时，还查阅此书以汲取精神力量。值得注意的是，车尔尼雪夫斯基创作这部小说部分是为了给自己的个人生活定义一种行为准则。他小说英雄的追求和议题也是他生活中的问题，两者最终都致力于历史的进步。

At the origins of this thinking about the new man was a novel by the nineteenth-century writer and critic Nikolai Chernyshevsky, entitled What Is to Be Done?, which provided an influential portrayal of the “new people”—young men and women distinguished by their ability to lead completely rationalist lives and wholeheartedly dedicate themselves to the revolution. Each of these “people of the new age” was a “strong personality”: “bold, unwavering, relentless, capable of taking matters in hand and of holding onto them tightly so they do not slip from his fingers.” One distant day these revolutionaries would become everyday types, but at present (in 1863) they were “rare specimens”: “They are like theine in tea, like the bouquet of a fine wine; they are its strength and fragrance. They are the flowers of the best people, the primal sources of energy, the salt of the salt of the earth!”

Chernyshevsky composed What Is to Be Done? as a call for action, and it was received as precisely that. Scores of radical students in late tsarist Russia molded themselves in the image of the novel; Lenin spoke of it as the single most important book in his life; as late as 1933 the Comintern head Georgi Dimitrov, accused by the Nazis of masterminding the fire at the Reichstag, consulted the book to gather spiritual strength while he awaited trial in a Berlin prison. Significantly, Chernyshevsky produced the novel in part to define a norm of behavior for his own personal life. The pursuits and issues of his novelistic heroes were also the questions of his life, and both were ultimately dedicated to history’s progress.

新人最决定性的品质，也是任何具有批判思维的人最应具备的品质，就是意识。意识集中在模范个人——作家、评论家、思想家——身上，它使人能够看清历史规律，理解自己作为历史行动主体所具有的潜能，并帮助开辟通往更美好未来的道路。这种理解奠定了道德行动的基础：它激发了意志，并赋予了为实现理想而不懈努力的愿望。历史规律是社会解放的规律；因此意识具有根本的社会取向，它激励个人代表受压迫群众思考和行动，从而创造出一种扩大的个人自我感，充满目的、意义和道德价值。意识的理性清晰是在个人与黑暗和混乱力量的斗争中获得的，无论是在社会世界还是在个人内心。这种秩序和清晰的标准是拥有一种“和谐的社会世界观”，这种世界观将个人置于“正确和公正的道路”上，并标志着他“新生活”的开始。在某种意义上，意识正是生命的衡量标准。在发展出揭示光明的世界观之前，你并不算完整地活着。

The decisive quality of the new man, and the most important quality for any critically thinking person to espouse, was consciousness. Concentrated in exemplary individuals—writers, critics, ideologues— consciousness was the ability to see the laws of history and comprehend one’s own potential as a subject of historical action who would help chart the road toward a better future. This understanding grounded moral action: it fueled the will and imparted the desire to work untiringly for the realization of the ideal. The laws of history were laws of social emancipation; hence the fundamentally social orientation of consciousness, which spurred the individual to think and act on behalf of the oppressed masses and thus created an enlarged sense of individual self, filled with purpose, significance, and moral value. The rational clarity of consciousness was attained in personal struggle against dark and chaotic forces, in the social world as well as within the individual. The criterion for such order and clarity was the possession of a “harmonious social worldview” that situated the individual on the “correct and just path” and signified the beginning of his “new life.” In some sense consciousness was the very measure of life. You did not fully live before developing a worldview that disclosed the light.

正是为了追求意识，德米特里·富尔曼诺夫在日记中开始追溯历史在他的个人生活中的运作。在1919年12月下旬的一篇回顾性条目中，他审视了自革命爆发以来的发展；尽管发展并不平衡，但他注意到一种从自发性到意识、从“童年、热情、无知”到“勇气、冷静、更高的意识和更多的知识”的明显成长。从根本上说，他认为革命将他造就成了一个充分发展的人。在政治觉醒之前，他过着“空虚、愚蠢、不严肃”的生活：“只有在革命的日子里，我才如梦初醒；在那之前我完全是个婴儿。”
意识的概念引导人们从传记的角度思考自己。从黑暗走向光明的旅程是从无到完整人性的旅程；它表现为一个内在化的、心理化的自我不断自我揭示的过程。正如富尔曼诺夫的案例所示，意识创造了具有非凡吸引力的自传叙事，因为它一方面强调社会激活和自我转型，另一方面强调心理探索和自我监控。

It was in pursuit of consciousness that Dmitri Furmanov set out in his diary to trace the workings of history in his personal life. In a retrospective entry in late December 1919 he surveyed his development since the outbreak of the revolution; despite its uneven character, he noticed a distinct growth from spontaneity to consciousness, from “childhood, enthusiasm, ignorance” to “courage, calm, greater consciousness and greater knowledge.” In a basic sense, he thought, the revolution had made him into a developed human being. He had led an “empty, stupid, unserious” existence prior to his political awakening: “Only during the days of revolution did the scales fall from my eyes; I was a complete infant up to then.”

The concept of consciousness invited thinking about oneself in biographical terms. The journey from darkness to light was a journey from non-being to full humanity; it proceeded as a growing self-disclosure of an interiorized, psychological self. As Furmanov’s case suggests, consciousness created autobiographical narratives of exceptional appeal, given its twofold emphasis on social activation and self-transformation on the one hand, and psychological exploration and self-monitoring on the other.

从列宁创建布尔什维克党的那一刻起，该党就将自己定义为革命意识的集中体现。该党由紧密团结的职业地下工作者圈子组成，结合了对革命的最高承诺和对每个成员异常自律的要求。在1917年10月夺取政权后，该党扩展了其使命，旨在传播其意识形态并将越来越广泛的人口阶层争取到共产主义事业中来。在寻求使意识成为一种普遍体验的过程中，布尔什维克展开了一场宏大的自我改造工程，其方式与富尔曼诺夫在日记中描述的自我转型大体相似。挑战在于使他们的追随者像布尔什维克——以及整个激进知识分子——看待自己那样思考和行动：作为生活受革命制约的历史主体。共产主义活动家不仅关心改变个人的外在态度；他们寻求占有他们的灵魂，即他们希望个人能理解共产党的历史使命并出于自身意志拥护它。贯穿始终的是一种唯意志论的假设，即革命的成败取决于激励其追随者的意识程度，取决于他们在多大程度上承认自己的生活在本质上是历史性的并据此行动。

From the moment it was founded by Lenin, the Bolshevik party defined itself as the concentrated expression of revolutionary consciousness. Composed of a tightly woven circle of professional underground workers, the party combined highest commitment to the revolution with a mandate of exceptional self-discipline on the part of every member. After assuming power in October 1917, the party extended its mission to disseminate its ideology and win over ever larger segments of the population to the Communist cause. In seeking to make consciousness a universal experience, the Bolsheviks deployed a gigantic project of self-change, much along the lines of the self-transformation described by Furmanov in his diary. The challenge was to make their followers think and act as the Bolsheviks—and the radical intelligentsia as a whole—saw themselves: as historical subjects whose lives were conditioned by the revolution. Communist activists were not solely concerned with changing individuals’ outward attitudes; they sought to appropriate their souls, in the sense that they wanted them to understand the historical mission of the Communist party and embrace it out of their own will. Throughout there was a voluntaristic assumption at work, which stipulated that the success or failure of the revolution hinged on the degree of consciousness animating its followers, on the extent to which they recognized their lives as historical in essence and acted on that recognition.
布尔什维克是语言帝国主义者；他们与马克思一样承认“存在决定意识”，因此工人需要革命剧本的力量来完全理解他的历史使命。在共产主义的理解中，革命语言不仅具有指称意义；正如托洛茨基所说，它是“思想本身的心脏……意识的形态本身”。苏联共产党人寻求在很大程度上通过语言手段来传播意识：通过阅读、书写以及口头和书面自我陈述的实践。
对这些实践的探索必须特别关注它们在布尔什维克历史想象中所占的位置。自始至终，布尔什维克的政策都受到一种对革命正在经历的历史阶段的敏锐感知的推动。在苏联马克思主义的理解中，人是一个历史进化着的生物。正如一位20世纪30年代的心理学家所说，“人的一切，从他的意识到他机体的每一个细胞，都是历史发展的产物。”

The Bolsheviks were verbal imperialists; they granted, with Marx, that “being determined consciousness” and that therefore the worker needed the power of the revolutionary script to fully understand his historical mission. Revolutionary language in Communist understanding had more than referential significance; it was, as Trotsky put it, the “heart of the ideas themselves . . . the very shape of consciousness.” Soviet Communists sought to impart consciousness in great measure by linguistic means: through practices of reading, writing, and oral and written self-presentation.

An exploration of these practices must pay particular attention to the place they occupied in the Bolsheviks’ historical imagination. All along, Bolshevik policies were motivated by an acute sense of the historical stages through which the revolution was passing. Man, in Soviet Marxist understanding, was a historically evolving being. As a psychologist of the 1930s put it, “all of man, from his consciousness to every cell of his organism, is a product of historical development.”
如果意识在本质上是历史性的，它就分阶段展开，这与作为历史执行者的苏联政权的独特政治阶段相对应。意识不是现成的、普遍存在的；相反，它必须通过艰苦的政治努力来传播，并逐渐占据个人，首先控制其环境和外在行为，然后进入其心理的深处。列夫·托洛茨基——写于1923年——在描绘革命已经走过以及为实现社会主义未来仍需跨越的阶段时，指出了这种由外而内的动态：

人类首先将黑暗元素从工业和意识形态中驱逐出去，以科学技术取代野蛮的惯例，用科学取代了宗教。随后，他通过用民主和理性主义议会制，继而用清晰公开的苏维埃专政推翻君主制和阶级，将无意识从政治中驱逐出去。盲目的元素在经济关系中积淀最深，但人类也正通过经济生活的社会主义组织将它们从中驱逐出去……最后，人类自身的本性隐藏在无意识、本能和底层最深、最黑暗的角落。探索性思考与创造性实践的最大努力将投向这一方向，难道不是不言自明的吗？

If consciousness was historical in nature, it unfolded in historical stages, which corresponded to distinct political phases of the Soviet regime as the executor of history. Consciousness was not ready-made and universally present; rather, it had to be disseminated by arduous political effort, and it gradually took hold of the individual, first controlling his environment and outward behavior, and then entering the recesses of his psyche. Leon Trotsky—writing in 1923—pointed to this dynamic of working from the outside in, as he charted the stages the revolution had traversed and had yet to cross to realize the socialist future:

Man first drove the dark elements out of industry and ideology, by displacing barbarian routine by scientific technique, and religion by science. Afterwards he drove the unconscious out of politics, by overthrowing monarchy and class with democracy and rationalist parliamentarianism and then with the clear and open Soviet dictatorship. The blind elements have settled most heavily in economic relations, but man is driving them out from there also, by means of the Socialist organization of economic life . . . Finally, the nature of man himself is hidden in the deepest and darkest corner of the unconscious, of the elemental, of the sub-soil. Is it not self-evident that the greatest efforts of investigative thought and of creative initiative will be in that direction?

凭借对自我主宰和个人意志的强调，“意识”具有揭示丰富的个人文化，甚至是浪漫主义心灵广阔领域的潜力。托洛茨基将社会主义的未来描述为一个“普通”人都能“升至亚里士多德、歌德或马克思的高度”的时代。然而，这种自我激活的图景只有在经历了一个漫长的动员和纪律性暴力的历史阶段后才能实现，这一阶段唤起的启蒙精神远多于浪漫主义精神。在内战结束后的十年里，布尔什维克活动家将苏维埃政权描绘为一种开明的专政。甚至列宁著名的“全俄电气化”口号也透露出共产党对自身的理解：作为一个光明的承载者，其使命是将教育和技术带给俄罗斯“黑暗”的群众。

With its stress on self-mastery and the individual will, consciousness had the potential to disclose a rich culture of the individual and, indeed, the expanse of a Romantic mind. Trotsky described the socialist future as a time when “average” people would “rise to the heights of an Aristotle, a Goethe, or a Marx.” Yet this scenario of self-activation could be realized only after a prolonged historical phase of mobilization and disciplinary violence which evoked the spirit of the Enlightenment much more than that of Romanticism. During the decade after the end of the civil war, Bolshevik activists cast Soviet power as an enlightened dictatorship. Even Lenin’s famous slogan of “electrifying the whole state” betrayed the self-understanding of the Communist party as a bearer of light whose mission was to bring education and technology to Russia’s “dark” masses.
从1930年代初开始，党领导层支持向浪漫主义感性的重大转变。这意味着，电气化已经取得了如此大的进步，以至于苏维埃公民自己也开始闪耀光芒。意识不再仅仅是强加给落后人民的东西；它已开始从内部展开，以越来越深的程度激励着越来越多的苏维埃公民。

富尔曼诺夫于1926年去世，他坚定地信奉共产主义事业的启蒙阶段。1918年加入布尔什维克党后，他成为共产主义意识的主要传播者。他被任命为政治委员，被派往一个由游击团组成的师担任意识形态督导，负责监管他们传奇的农民指挥官瓦西里·恰巴耶夫（夏伯阳）。富尔曼诺夫在这些年里一直坚持写日记，后来根据他与恰巴耶夫的相遇写了一部纪实小说。在日记和小说中，这种关系都是通过“原始自发性”与“革命意识”的二元对立来讲述的。恰巴耶夫是一位精神抖擞但缺乏纪律的领导者。他的无政府主义精神必须经过引导和组织，才能为革命服务，并对历史有用。这就是政治委员的任务，在小说中他的名字叫费奥多尔·克雷奇科夫。克雷奇科夫总是以完美的理性主义语言思考和交谈，他的言语把体力强健但智力薄弱的恰巴耶夫塑造得“像蜡一样”。然而，如果将恰巴耶夫和克雷奇科夫视为一对，他们则融合了行动主义与意识、民间机智与知识分子文化的革命品质。考虑到富尔曼诺夫本人在1917年曾倾向于无政府主义立场，以及他在日记中对自己混乱心理进行的斗争，小说中的两位主角可以看作是作者为成为革命自觉主体而进行的个人斗争的体现。富尔曼诺夫遵循车尔尼雪夫斯基的传统创作了小说《恰巴耶夫》，这是一个以自传为灵感的、值得效仿的模范革命者的故事。当《恰巴耶夫》于1923年出版时，它立即成为了畅销书，并为后来几十部苏维埃小说设定了标准，这些小说对自发性与意识之间同样的紧张关系进行了各种变体演绎。

富尔曼诺夫的内战著作清楚地表明，新生的苏维埃政权在话语的战场上投入了多少精力。《恰巴耶夫》中描述的红军士兵明白，“战争不仅要靠刺刀来进行并赢得胜利，还要靠明智、新鲜的语言，清醒的头脑，以及把握整个局势并根据需要向他人传达其意义的能力。”富尔曼诺夫参加了1919年6月从白军手中夺回乌法市的战斗。攻占该市后几小时内，“大量传单分发给居民，解释形势。墙报覆盖了房屋的墙壁，从第二天早上起，师报每天早晨定期出版。在城镇的各个角落都举行了即兴集会。”

“我们的语言是我们最好的武器，”红军全军军事训练管理局局长尼古拉·波德沃伊斯基宣布。言语具有“瓦解”敌人“灵魂，瘫痪其神经，将其分裂为敌对阵营和阶级派系”的力量。但言语也可以向个人传授大整体的意识，并将其塑造成集体机体的微粒。最重要的是，革命话语具有强烈的传记吸引力；它们在阶级斗争、解放、教育和赋权的宏大叙事中创造了个人线索，从而使革命信息与那些被宣讲的对象产生关联。“他们进行着不间断的宣传，”一位白军军官说道，勉强承认了红军政治工作者在招募的人员中开展活动的成功，“[他们]利用每一个可用的机会，甚至[利用]最微小的事实来强调布尔什维克政权给他们的生活带来的好处。”

Starting in the early 1930s, the party leadership endorsed a momentous shift toward a Romantic sensibility. Electrification, it implied, had made such progress that Soviet citizens themselves were beginning to shine. Consciousness was no longer simply imposed on backward people; it had begun to unfold from within, animating Soviet citizens in ever greater numbers and deeper measure.

Furmanov, who died in 1926, firmly adhered to the Enlightenment stage of the Communist project. After joining the Bolshevik party in 1918 he became a leading disseminator of Communist consciousness. Appointed political commissar, he was dispatched to a division of partisan regiments as an ideological supervisor for their legendary peasant commander, Vassily Chapaev. Furmanov, who kept his diary throughout these years, later wrote a documentary novel about his encounter with Chapaev. In both the diary and the novel the relationship is told through the binary opposition of elementary spontaneity and revolutionary consciousness. Chapaev was a spirited but undisciplined leader. His anarchistic spirit had to be channeled and organized in order to serve the revolution and be of use to history. This was the task of the political commissar, who in the novel bears the name Fedor Klychkov. Klychkov always thinks and speaks in a perfectly rationalist idiom, and his speech molds Chapaev, who is physically strong but in-tellectually weak, “like wax.” If considered as a pair, however, Chapaev and Klychkov fuse the revolutionary qualities of activism and consciousness, popular resourcefulness and intelligentsia culture. In light of Furmanov’s own flirtation with anarchist positions in 1917 and the campaigns he conducted in his diary against his own disorganized psyche, the two leading actors in the novel read as a representation of the author’s personal struggle to become a conscious subject of the revolution. Furmanov wrote the novel, Chapaev, in Chernyshevsky’s tradition, as an autobiographically inspired story of exemplary revolutionaries who were to be emulated. When Chapaev was published in 1923 it became an instant bestseller and set the standard for scores of later Soviet novels that would offer variations on the same tension between spontaneity and consciousness.

Furmanov’s civil war writings make clear how much effort the nascent Soviet regime expended on the rhetorical battlefield. The Red Army soldiers described in Chapaev understood that “the war had to be waged and won, not only at the point of a bayonet, but by means of wise, fresh words, a clear mind, and the ability to grasp the entire situation and convey its meaning to others as required.” Furmanov took part in the recapturing of the city of Ufa from the Whites in June 1919. Within hours after the storming of the city, “a huge quantity of leaflets were distributed among the population, explaining the situation. Wall newspapers covered the walls of the houses, and from the morning of the next day on, the divisional newspaper was regularly issued every morning. Improvised meetings were held in all corners of the town.”

“Our word is our best weapon,” declared Nikolai Podvoisky, head of the Red Army’s universal military training administration. Words had the power to “disintegrate” the enemy’s “soul, paralyze his nerves, split him into warring camps and class factions.” But words could also impart to individuals the consciousness of a larger whole and mold them into particles of a collective body. Most important, revolutionary words had an intense biographical appeal; they created personal threads in a larger narrative of class struggle, emancipation, education, and empowerment, and thereby made the revolutionary message relevant to those to whom it was preached. “They conduct unceasing agitation,” a White officer said, grudgingly acknowledging the success with which the Red Army’s political workers campaigned among their recruits; “[they take] advantage of every available opportunity and [exploit] even the most trivial fact to highlight the benefits that the Bolshevik regime has brought to their lives.”

苏维埃政权在1920年进行的一次普查确定，60%的成年人口不会读写。在这种条件下，宣传政治语言力量的能力取决于建立基础识字能力。苏维埃国家坚持不懈地开展识字运动，明确旨在灌输革命意识。1919年12月颁布的关于扫盲的政府法令开篇宣言如下：“为了让共和国全体人民自觉地参与国家的政治生活，人民委员会法令规定……”该法令以数十万份传单的形式分发，命令所有8至50岁之间的文盲公民学习。列宁表达了同样的要求：“文盲站在政治之外。首先必须教他字母表。没有它，就只有传闻、童话、偏见，而没有政治。”反对文盲的斗争是“政治的前提”。
读写的技术能力与创造具有政治素养的公民的议程密不可分。政治启蒙工作是为了培养“积极且自觉”的苏维埃公民，为了“唤醒积极性”并“灌输积极行动的习惯”。

A census carried out by the Soviet regime in 1920 established that 60 percent of the adult population could not read and write. Under these conditions, the ability to preach the power of political language depended on establishing elementary literacy. The literacy campaigns relentlessly conducted by the Soviet state were explicitly aimed at inculcating a revolutionary consciousness. The government decree on illiteracy issued in December 1919 opened with the following declaration: “For the purpose of allowing the entire population of the Republic to participate consciously in the political life of the country, the Council of People’s Commissars decrees . . .” Distributed in hundreds of thousands of leaflets, the decree ordered all illiterate citizens between the ages of 8 and 50 to study. Lenin formulated the same imperative: “The illiterate person stands outside of politics. First it is necessary to teach him the alphabet. Without it there are only rumors, fairy tales, prejudices, but not politics.” The struggle against illiteracy was a “precondition of politics.”

The technical ability to read and write was inextricably linked to the agenda of creating politically literate citizens. The work of political enlightenment was to raise “active and conscious” Soviet citizens, to “awaken activity” and “instill the habit of being active.”
在第一次五年计划的“文化长征”期间，此时已成为社会主义国家热心支持者的马克西姆·高尔基向苏维埃公众发出呼吁，为成人教育捐款：“同志们，帮帮忙！每一卢布都将为那些想要学习的人提供铅笔和笔记本，以便以更大的精力和更清晰的意识建设新生活。”

为了提高个人的意识，苏维埃活动家制定了明确的读写准则。正如他们所强调的，这些过程不应盲目地发展。阅读和写作不应死记硬背地进行；相反，它们应该是创造性自我投入的实例。一位在1920年代写作的苏维埃教育家建议，“自觉阅读”应成为红军士兵培训的一部分：“理性阅读的第一条规则应该是其充分的意识；……对于一个自觉的读者来说，一本书不应是现成思想的源泉，而应是一个人自己思想的材料，仅仅是促进一个人在某一学科中进行严肃、独立的工作。”作者们强调了“独立”获得政治素养的重要性：“为了真正具备政治素养，仅仅研读社会科学的理论和历史著作是不够的。人们还必须能够独立地将获得的材料应用于当代生活。有必要在当前的政治生活中定位自己。”在要求个人独立参与文本的过程中，教育工作者认为意识的概念必须从个人内部产生，而不能从外部强加。同样，苏维埃学校的课程强调，作业应该发挥学生独立的创造能力。完成某项作业“不仅应该训练和教育学生的智力，还应该锻炼他的意志。”

During the “cultural crusade” of the First Five-Year Plan, Maxim Gorky, by now an ardent supporter of the socialist state, issued a plea to the Soviet public to donate money for adult education: “Help, comrades! Every ruble will give pencils and notebooks to people who want to study in order to build the new life with greater energy and a clearer consciousness.”

As part of the drive to raise individuals’ consciousness, Soviet activists devised clear precepts on how to read and write. As they emphasized, these processes should not evolve thoughtlessly. Reading and writing were not to be done by rote; on the contrary, they were to be instances of creative self-investment. A Soviet educator, writing in the 1920s, recommended that “conscious reading” be part of the training of Red Army soldiers: “The first rule of rational reading should be its full consciousness; . . . for a conscious reader, a book ought not to be a source of ready-formed ideas, but material for one’s own thoughts, only facilitating one’s serious, independent work in this or that discipline.” Authors stressed the importance of acquiring political literacy “independently”: “In order to truly be politically literate, it is not enough to work through the theoretical and historical books in the social sciences. One must still be able to independently apply the acquired material to contemporary life. It is necessary to orient oneself in current political life.” In demanding that texts be engaged individually and independently, educators argued that the notion of consciousness had to arise from within individuals and could not be enforced from outside. Similarly, the Soviet school curriculum emphasized that assignments should bring out students’ independent, creative abilities. Work on a given assignment “should train and educate not only the student’s intellect, but also his will.”

布尔什维克在内战中取得了胜利，但代价是这个国家遭受了七年战争的蹂躏。苏维埃国家不得不应对因战争、疾病及其自身不加区别的暴力而造成的数百万生命损失。此外，这个国家的城市和工业中心——对“无产阶级专政”至关重要的资源——已元气大伤；大多数工人已经离开闲置或被毁的工厂回到家乡。在布尔什维克的解释中，这表明党的中坚力量中革命意识出现了令人担忧的下降。鉴于这些损失，该政权别无选择，只能勉强接受经济中的私营部门。新经济政策（NEP）在党的领导人及其追随者中引起了巨大的焦虑，他们担心数百万小规模生产者和贸易商所体现的小资产阶级意识会污染并致命地腐蚀苏维埃社会年轻的革命心灵。在新经济政策期间，旧世界力量的强大复兴抑制了除最热心的革命者外所有人的转型雄心。大多数布尔什维克将这一意识形态妥协时期解释为暂时退却，以便为对资本主义制度的决定性进攻重新积聚力量。

The Bolsheviks emerged victorious from the civil war, but at the cost of a country ravaged by seven years of war. The Soviet state had to cope with the loss of millions of lives due to warfare, diseases, and its own indiscriminate violence. Moreover, the country’s urban and industrial centers, vital resources for the “dictatorship of the proletariat,” were depleted; most of their workers had left the idle or destroyed factories to return to their home villages. In Bolshevik interpretation this indicated an alarming drop in revolutionary consciousness among the party’s mainstays. In view of these losses, the regime had no choice but to grudgingly accept a private sector in the economy. The New Economic Policy (NEP) created great anxieties among party leaders and their followers, who feared that the petit-bourgeois consciousness embodied by millions of small-scale producers and traders would contaminate and fatally corrupt the young revolutionary mind of Soviet society. The powerful resurgence during the NEP of forces from the old world dampened the transformative ambitions of all but the most ardent revolutionaries. Most Bolsheviks interpreted this period of ideological compromise as a temporary retreat in order to regain momentum for the decisive assault on the capitalist system.

为了在未加改造的俄罗斯农民世界这片沼泽和新经济政策时期资产阶级的繁华世界中保持自身完整，党收紧了队伍，将自己视为一座四面受敌的意识堡垒。从1921年开始的一系列清洗——正是在苏维埃国家采纳新经济政策时——是为了测试每个党员的意识形态纯洁性。除了“无产阶级的公敌”、反革命政党雇佣的“特务和挑衅者”之外，清洗的目标还包括那些“小资产阶级”自私自利者，他们加入党是为了“个人利益[而非]无产阶级斗争和革命的利益”。警惕的共产党员可以通过看穿这些人对集体事业至多是表面的坚持来识别这类人。由于性格“软弱”且“无原则”，他们缺乏意志力来克制自己对自我满足的本能渴望，并且无法察觉那些随意操纵他们的敌人的计谋。在清除这些不合格元素的同时，党表彰并肯定了那些经受住审查并表现出“奉献精神、耐力、政治成熟度和牺牲精神”的人，正如一份党的决议所定义的共产主义意识的本质。清洗旨在成为推动共产党员“上演他们自己的‘十月’[革命]”的动力。他们被要求利用对其纯洁性的考验来“审视自己，并在布尔什维克好扫帚的帮助下，扫除内心的小资产阶级……学会理解集体的意志和利益，并以此定义自己的意志和利益——这是创造新生活的第一步。”

共产党员的主观本质，其性格的强弱，在他向党内同志陈述的“自传”中表现出来，这是清洗过程的戏剧性高潮时刻。自传这一体裁产生于共产党内部，但在1920年代的过程中，它传播到了共青团和非党机构。每个申请成为大学生或在政府机构工作的苏维埃公民都必须写一份自传。此外，公民被要求在他们的整个生命周期中定期重新提交自传。因此，可以稳妥地假设，大多数成年苏维埃公民不仅熟悉这种自我陈述的形式及其随附的规则，而且熟悉其潜在假设：他们的传记会根据革命的进程及其自身主观政治意识的发展而被重写。

To remain intact in the swamp of unreformed peasant Russia and the glittering world of the NEP bourgeoisie, the party closed its ranks, conceiving of itself as an embattled bastion of consciousness. A series of purges, beginning in 1921, just when the Soviet state had adopted the NEP, were to test the ideological purity of each party member. Besides “outright enemies of the proletariat,” “agents and provocateurs” hired by counterrevolutionary parties, the purges targeted those “petit-bourgeois” self-seekers who had joined the party out of concern for “their personal well-being [rather] than the interests of proletarian struggle and revolution.” The vigilant Communist could recognize these types by seeing through their at best superficial adherence to the collective cause. “Weak” and “unprincipled” in character, they lacked the willpower to master their instinctual craving for self-gratification and were unable to discern the ploys of enemies who manipulated them at will. While eliminating these unfit elements, the party honored and validated those who withstood its scrutiny and demonstrated “dedication, endurance, political maturity, and readiness to sacrifice [themselves],” as a party resolution defined the essence of Communist consciousness. The purge was to serve as an impetus for Communists to “stage their own ‘October’ [Revolution].” They were called upon to use the test of their purity to “look into themselves and, with the help of a good Bolshevik broom, to sweep out the petit-bourgeois within . . . To learn to understand the will, the interests of the collective, and to define one’s own will and interests by them—this is a first step to creating a new life.”

The Communist’s subjective essence, the strength or weakness of his character, came to the fore in his “autobiography,” which he recited to his party comrades in the climactic dramatic moment of the purge process. The autobiography emerged in the Communist party milieu, but in the course of the 1920s it spread to the Komsomol and non-party institutions. Every Soviet citizen who applied to become a university student or to work in a government agency had to compose an autobiography. Moreover, citizens were required to resubmit their autobiographies at recurrent intervals throughout their lives. It is therefore safe to assume that most adult Soviet citizens were familiar, not only with this genre of self-presentation and its attendant rules, but also with the underlying assumption that their biographies were subject to rewriting, in accordance with the progression of the revolution and the development of their own, subjective political consciousness.

自传是对某个共产党员生活的简短散文描述，列出了教育和职业成就，但其核心重点是作者人格作为革命意识之主体的形成。虽然这种公开自我陈述行为的主题和重点遵循既定指南，但自传保留了一个重要的主观维度，因为个人必须令人信服地展示他们走向共产主义光明的旅程路径。这些自我叙述通常以主观蒙昧的深渊为出发点，以更好地突出随后向苏维埃事业的皈依以及所走过的路程距离。一个人在多大程度上能向听众传达他内心是一个社会主义公民，最终决定了他是否能被接纳加入共产党。

1920年代的共产主义自传是以自我否定形式进行的自我表达姿态。理想的共产党员——见富尔曼诺夫/克雷奇科夫——是革命的扩音器，比起拥有表达性灵魂的浪漫主义主体，他更像一台机器。事实上，1920年代的革命活动家经常将人类的理想型塑造成机器式的人。电影导演济加·维尔托夫梦想着一种“完美的电气人”——一个灵魂不再受混乱心理冲动支配，而是像机械一样以定向的能量和精度运作的人：“新人，摆脱了笨重和笨拙，将拥有机器般的轻盈、精准动作。”如果革命意识被定义为极端的纪律和作为大整体的一部分不知疲倦地运作的能力，那么机器就是这种意识的衡量标准。

1920年代积极征集的另一种传记媒介是十月革命的回忆录。从意识形态受污染的新经济政策时期的角度来看，革命精神在1917年10月似乎是最纯洁的。共产党新成立的历史部门邀请1917年的老战士撰写关于他们如何参与并制造布尔什维克革命的回忆录。这一举措引来了大量关于1917年的其他个人回忆，许多来稿“文字粗陋、写得很差”。正是通过这些叙述，参与者才拥有了革命——几乎不管他们在1917年的实际角色如何：关于那个十月的一些自传叙述是从1917年并未发生布尔什维克起义的地区寄来的。无论真实还是虚构，这些例子都传达了将自己写入革命叙事的吸引力。

A short account in prose of a given Communist’s life, the autobiography listed educational and professional achievements, but at its core it focused on the formation of its author’s personality as an unfolding subject of revolutionary consciousness. While the themes and emphases in this act of public self-presentation followed established guidelines, the autobiography retained an important subjective dimension, because individuals had to convincingly lay out the paths of their journeys toward the Communist light. Often these self-narratives took their point of departure in an abyss of subjective tenebrosity, to better highlight both the ensuing conversion toward the Soviet cause and the distance of the route traveled. The degree to which an individual could convey to the audience that he was a socialist citizen at heart ultimately decided his admission to the Communist party.

The Communist autobiography of the 1920s was a gesture of self-expression in the form of self-abnegation. The ideal Communist—witness Furmanov/Klychkov—was a loudspeaker of the revolution and re-sembled a machine more than a Romantic subject with an expressive soul. Indeed, revolutionary activists of the 1920s frequently cast the ideal type of humanity in the form of a machine man. The filmmaker Dziga Vertov dreamed of a “perfect electric man”—one whose soul was no longer subject to chaotic psychological impulses but functioned with the directed energy and precision of machinery: “The New Man, free of unwieldiness and clumsiness, will have the light, precise movements of machines.” If revolutionary consciousness was defined as utter discipline and the ability to tirelessly function as part of a larger whole, the machine was the measure of such consciousness.

Another biographical medium actively solicited during the 1920s was the memoir of the October Revolution. From the vantage point of the ideologically polluted NEP period, the revolutionary spirit appeared to have been at its purest in October 1917. A newly founded history section of the Communist party invited veterans of 1917 to produce memoirs about how they had participated in, and made, the Bolshevik revolution. This initiative sparked a spontaneous influx of other personal reminiscences about 1917, many of them “illiterate and poorly written.” It was through these narratives that participants came to own the revolution—almost regardless of their actual roles in 1917: some autobiographical accounts of that October were sent in from regions that had not witnessed a Bolshevik uprising in 1917. No matter how truthful or fictitious, these instances convey the appeal of inscribing oneself into the revolutionary narrative.

然而，共产主义自传和革命回忆录的吸引力都受到对1917年作为革命意识决定性门槛这一执念的限制。在1920年代末，当斯大林领导下的苏维埃政权发动第二次革命并着手建设新的社会主义世界时，这种执念被克服了。苏维埃活动家现在宣布，自1917年10月以来的几年里，革命已经成熟——它在追随者中产生了足够程度的意识，足以将未来变为现实。苏维埃制度被认为足够强大，政府可以着手打破阶级社会，建立无阶级的社会主义秩序。这意味着一个完全自觉的主体出现了，他将居住在无阶级社会中，这个充分形成的人所提供的能量，则将推动工业化。斯大林主义国家的理想是唯意志论的；它优先考虑个人而非集体作为界定人类行为的基本实体；它还恢复了个人灵魂作为自觉意志的基础。斯大林主义意识形态机构培养个人传记，强调杰出人格的塑造，而非无生命机器的卓越行为。

Yet the appeal of both the Communist autobiography and the revolutionary memoir was limited by a fixation on 1917 as the decisive threshold of revolutionary consciousness. In the late 1920s, when the Soviet regime under Stalin’s leadership launched a second revolution and set out to build the new socialist world, this fixation was overcome. Soviet activists now proclaimed that in the years since October 1917 the revolution had come of age—it had produced a sufficient degree of consciousness among its followers to will the future into being. The Soviet system was deemed sufficiently strong for the government to proceed with the breakup of class society and the creation of a classless socialist order. This meant that a fully conscious subject had appeared, who was to inhabit the classless society, and the energy provided by this fully formed individual was to fuel the drive for industrialization. The ideal of the Stalinist state was voluntarist; it privileged the individual rather than the collective as the defining basic entity of human behavior; it also rehabilitated the individual soul as the basis of the conscious will. The Stalinist ideological apparatus cultivated individual biographies, emphasizing the making of exceptional personalities rather than the exceptional deeds of inanimate machines.

马克西姆·高尔基在创造斯大林政权的“新人”方面发挥了关键作用。高尔基是一位具有强烈尼采倾向的作家，他希望革命能开创一种社会秩序，释放人天生的英雄本质，使人得以过上一种新的、丰富的、充满活力的、美好的生活。高尔基曾在1920年代初离开俄罗斯，在1931年正式定居苏联之前，他曾于1928年和1929年两次访问苏联，均受到广泛报道。他写道，他对在苏维埃人口中观察到的心理变化感到惊讶。人们正沉浸在政治思想中，“政治意识”正在成为“一种日常现象”。“每个人在本质上都变得更年轻了。”高尔基刻意将这一形象与他回忆起革命前在同样地方旅行时的感受形成对比：“俄罗斯式的虚弱和精神上的哀伤”以及“俄罗斯特有的忧郁倾向”。
“新人”是历史的产物，更具体地说是斯大林领导层发起的为实现社会主义社会而进行的“世界历史性”运动的产物。在呼吁苏维埃公民参与集体建设新世界时，领导层诉诸于他们的英雄气质。这种气质激发了他们的理性主义热情、乐观的自信和创造性能量——这些都是斯大林主义新人的核心特征，与资产阶级西方的“旧人”形成鲜明对比，后者是自私、原子化且反进步的。

Maxim Gorky played an instrumental role in creating the new man of the Stalinist regime. A writer with strong Nietzschean leanings, Gorky hoped that the revolution would inaugurate a social order that would release man’s inborn heroic essence and allow him to live a new, rich, vital, and beautiful life. Gorky, who had left Russia in the early 1920s, returned to the Soviet Union for two widely publicized visits, in 1928 and 1929, before settling there for good in 1931. He wrote of being amazed by the psychic changes he observed in the Soviet population. The people were saturating themselves with political ideas, and “political consciousness” was becoming “an everyday phenomenon.” “Everybody had become younger in essence.” Gorky placed this image in deliberate contrast to the sentiment he recalled from journeys to the same places before the revolution: “Russian feebleness and spiritual mourning” and the “specifically Russian bent for sadness.”

The new man was a product of history, more specifically the “world historical” campaign unleashed by the Stalinist leadership to bring a socialist society into being. In calling on Soviet citizens to involve themselves in the collective building of the new world, the leadership appealed to their heroic disposition. That disposition fueled their rationalist zeal, optimistic self-confidence, and creative energy—all central characteristics of the Stalinist new man, in explicit contrast to the “old man” of the bourgeois West, who was self-seeking, atomized, and antiprogressive.
然而，正如高尔基所坚持的，斯大林时代建设工地上的工人们尚未完全意识到他们时代的伟大及其包含的人类意义。文学的任务是提供一面“放大镜”，让他们在其中认识到自己是英雄现实的积极参与者。

在斯大林的支持下，高尔基将整个苏维埃作家职业导向了一个目标：为新人灌输社会主义意识，即“塑造他的灵魂”。高尔基和共产党领导层援引了追溯到车尔尼雪夫斯基的传统，呼吁苏维埃作家塑造模范英雄典型，供作家和读者效仿。然而，与过去的乌托邦小说不同，斯大林时期的“社会主义现实主义”艺术不是为了召唤未来的英雄。相反，它的任务是记录最优秀的苏维埃公民的惊人行为，同时赋予这些现实英雄以丰富的内心世界，这与他们作为社会主义时代的“完整人格”相称。文学要向新的苏维埃公民展示他们本质上是什么样的人，尽管他们尚未意识到这一点：具有无尽创造潜力的表达型个人。

Yet, as Gorky maintained, the workers on Stalin-era construction sites were as yet not fully aware of the greatness of their age and the human implications it held. The task of literature was to provide a “magnifying mirror,” in which they could comprehend themselves as active participants in a heroic reality.

With Stalin’s support, Gorky redirected the entire Soviet writing profession toward the goal of instilling a socialist consciousness into the new man, of “engineering his soul.” Invoking a tradition that went back to Chernyshevsky, Gorky and the Communist leadership called on Soviet writers to create exemplary heroic types to be emulated by the writers and their readers alike. Unlike the utopian novel of the past, however, “socialist realist” art of the Stalin period was not to evoke a future hero. Its task was instead to document the amazing deeds of the best Soviet citizens, while endowing these real heroes with the rich inner world that befitted them as “total personalities” of the socialist age. Literature was to show the new Soviet citizens what they were at essence but did not yet know they were: expressive individuals with endless creative potential.
对作为新人缩影的英雄个人的新关注，伴随着对传记模式的新崇拜。一份完整的传记，描绘从一无所有到拥有一切的轨迹，成为新人最切实的物质实体。鲍里斯·帕斯捷尔纳克在1934年苏维埃作家协会成立大会上呼吁使用一种诗意的“语言，来捕捉新苏维埃人民的现实——‘他们已经挣脱了财产的锚点，正在……在传记可构想的空间里自由翱翔’”。
传记——即使被延伸到其可想象的极限——也是社会主义人恰如其分的模子；它提供了一种生活被正确呈现和理解的形式。

The new attention to the heroic individual as epitome of the new man went along with a new veneration of the biographical mode. A full-fledged biography, delineating a trajectory from nothing to everything, served as the most tangible material substance of the new man. Boris Pasternak at the founding congress of the Soviet Writers’ Union in 1934 called for a poetic “language that would capture the reality of the new Soviet people, “who have torn themselves from the anchors of property and who are soaring freely . . . in the space of the biographically conceivable.”
Biography—even if stretched to its imaginable limit—was the fitting mold of socialist man; it provided the form in which a life was properly represented and understood.

高尔基积极推动苏维埃传记媒介。回到苏联后，他发起了一系列传记项目，其中最著名的是《工厂史》，以那些建设者的传记和自传叙述的形式记录了该国一百多家最大的企业。他依赖传记作为意识展开的叙述，这与早期的1917年集体记忆项目相似，但与该倡议不同的是，高尔基的项目试图将政治主体性与当下历史的展开联系起来，并呼吁每个工人成为自传主体。一种新的观念认为，斯大林主义建设中的每一个工人，通过将自己的命运与一个更大的工作集体和具有世界历史意义的转型事件联系起来，把自己放大到英雄般的、超人的尺度，正如高尔基所宣布的，成为大写的“人”（M-A-N）。

Gorky actively promoted the Soviet biographical medium. After returning to the Soviet Union he initiated a series of biographical projects, most notably the “History of the Factories,” a documentation of more than a hundred of the country’s largest enterprises in the form of biographical and autobiographical accounts of those who were building them. His reliance on biography as a narrative of unfolding consciousness resembled the earlier project of collective remembrance of 1917, but unlike that initiative, Gorky’s project sought to link political subjectivity to the unfolding of history in the present, and it appealed to every worker to become an autobiographical subject. There was a new sense that every worker in Stalinist construction, by tying his fate to a larger working collective and a transformative event of world historical proportions, enlarged himself to heroic, superhuman proportions, became, as Gorky declared, a “M-A-N with capital letters.”

斯大林时代最杰出的传记属于创纪录的采煤工、挤奶工和极地飞行员，他们的故事在1930年代激增。他们的事迹得到了意识形态机构的背书，该机构渴望识别出确认政权关于社会主义社会已真正形成之主张的个人英雄行为。在共产党看来，这些非凡成就之所以成为可能，是因为消除了新经济政策的资本主义结构，并建立了社会主义环境，使苏维埃公民能够自由发展其全部潜力，并体验到——正如布哈林所说——“创造力、物质充裕、文化成长、心理视野的拓宽、社会活动的增强、接触到越来越多的精神愉悦，以及感觉到他的力量和人格在不断增长。人格首次作为一种群众现象出现，而不仅仅作为其各种历史变体中的奴隶主上层阶级的一部分。”

剧作家亚历山大·阿菲诺格诺夫——在寻找斯大林时代英雄的众多文人之一——在日记中评论了斯达汉诺夫式采煤工伊万·古多夫的非凡事迹——古多夫的劳动成绩超过日常定额四十五倍——并把他比作艺术家，“一个艺术大师和天才”，并继续道：“古多夫是在我们土地上如此强劲绽放的社会主义天才的原型。这是一种全新的人的品质，一种产生于社会主义社会结构的品质。而且他绝非孤身一人！他们就在那里——迸发自由的人性能量原子。他们释放的能量是取之不尽的。而这使得他们生活的秩序无往不胜！”

The most outstanding biographies of the Stalinist age belonged to the record-setting coal miners, milkmaids, and polar aviators whose stories proliferated in the 1930s. Their exploits were underwritten by an ideological apparatus eager to identify acts of individual heroism that confirmed the regime’s claims that a socialist society had truly come into being. In the Communist view these singular achievements were made possible by the elimination of the capitalist structures of NEP and the establishment of a socialist environment that allowed the Soviet citizen to freely develop his full potential and to experience, as Bukharin put it, “creativity, material sufficiency, cultural growth, a broadening mental horizon, heightened social activity, exposure to an ever growing amount of spiritual pleasures, the sense that his powers and his personality is ever growing. The personality appears for the first time as a mass phenomenon and not just as part of the slave-owning upper class in its various historical variants.”

Commenting in his diary on the extraordinary feats of Ivan Gudov, a Stakhanovite coal miner who exceeded his daily labor quota by forty-five times, the playwright Alexander Afinogenov—one among many literati in search of Stalin-era heroes—likened him to an artist, “a virtuoso and a talent,” and went on: “Gudov is a prototype of the socialist talent which is flowering so powerfully in our land. This is a totally new quality of man, a quality that has been born of the socialist structure of society. And he is far from alone! There they are—atoms of human energy bursting into freedom. The radiation of their energy is inexhaustible. And this makes the order in which they live invincible!”

斯大林时代的新男性和新女性被赋予的品质在核心上是浪漫主义的。他们是丰富的人格个体，通过奇幻的事迹表达自己，其艺术创造力帮助塑造了美丽的社会主义新世界。他们的榜样取代并盖过了早期机器式的人的革命理想。如果说在苏维埃政权的头几年，泰勒制的狂热倡导者阿列克谢·加斯捷夫曾幻想着“没有灵魂的、毫无表情的面孔，它们不懂诗歌或情感，不为文字或笑声所动，而是由压力计和计程表来衡量”，那么斯达汉诺夫工作者则以其意志的炽热火焰挥舞着金属技术。与前几代被培养成苦行者、自我否定者的共产党员不同，他们拥有“情感、……激情”。
1930年代中期的“高斯大林主义”时期是苏维埃革命诉诸自我的顶峰。从早期坚持塑造和启蒙“广大群众”，重点已转向更强大、更复杂的个人灵魂语汇。1930年代的共产主义活动家号召苏维埃公民在为建设完美未来的集体项目做出贡献时表达其丰富的本质。

The qualities ascribed to the new men and women of the Stalinist age were Romantic to the core. They were rich personalities who expressed themselves in fantastic feats and whose artistic creativity helped shape the beautiful new socialist world. Their example superseded and eclipsed the earlier revolutionary ideal of the machine man. If during the first years of Soviet power Alexei Gastev, a fervent advocate of Taylorism, had fantasized about “expressionless faces without a soul, which know no poetry or emotions and which are not moved by writing or laughter, but are measured with manometer and taxometer,” the Stakhanovites wielded metal technology with the burning flame of their will. In contrast to the preceding generation of Communists, who had been reared as ascetic, self-denying beings, they had “feelings, . . . passions.”

The period of “high Stalinism” during the mid-1930s was the apotheosis of the Soviet revolutionary appeal to the self. From an earlier insistence on molding and enlightening the “broad masses,” the emphasis had shifted toward a more powerful and complex idiom of the individual soul. Communist activists of the 1930s called on Soviet citizens to express their rich essence in contributing to the collective project of building the perfect future.

斯大林将英雄的表达主义定义为苏维埃制度的核心属性。1938年3月，他会见了一个极地飞行员代表团，他们在浮冰上紧急着陆后奇迹般地获救。斯大林在向飞行员敬酒时宣布，欧洲国家和美国是根据金钱价值来评价其每一位公民的：“美国人会说一个英雄值10万美元。”相比之下，共产主义政府引入了一种新的“苏维埃式”评价人的方法，“不按卢布，也不按美元”。它依据人的“大胆才干和潜力”来评价人，正因如此，他们才完成了史无前例的事迹。斯大林暗示，苏联拥有与西方相同的飞机和现代技术，但它的地位远高于西方，因为它孕育了这样的人。西方虽然美元丰富，却缺乏评价人类天生英雄气概的货币。只有苏维埃政府承认人所代表的“巨额资本”。这种对人类英雄气概和灵魂表现力的押注，在苏维埃公民中激发了为苏维埃国家工作的强烈愿望，因为这种活动是衡量他们生活的标准。就像遇险的极地飞行员一样，苏维埃公民想要“斗争和生活，在工业、农业和文化的一切领域斗争；他们不想死，而是想活；为了活下去并击倒敌人；为了胜利而活下去”。

Stalin defined heroic expressivism as the central attribute of the Soviet system. In March 1938 he met with a delegation of polar aviators who had been spectacularly rescued following an emergency landing on drifting ice. European countries and the United States, Stalin declared in his toast to the pilots, judged every one of their citizens by his monetary worth: “Americans will say that a hero costs 100,000 dollars.” The Communist government, by contrast, had introduced a new, “Soviet,” “method of evaluating people, not in rubles, nor in dollars.” It appraised people by their “daring talent and potential,” thanks to which they accomplished unprecedented deeds. The Soviet Union, Stalin suggested, possessed the same planes and modern technology as the West, but it ranked far above the West because of the people it bred. Rich in dollars, the West lacked a currency to evaluate man’s innate heroism. Only the Soviet government acknowledged the “huge capital” that man represented. This wager on man’s heroism and the expressive resources of his soul unleashed an intense desire among Soviet citizens to work for the Soviet state because this activity was the measure of their life. Like the polar aviators in distress, Soviet citizens wanted to “struggle and live, struggle in all spheres of industry, agriculture, and culture; they did not want to die, but to live; to live and strike down the enemies; to live in order to prevail.”

斯大林的祝酒词揭示了无限的可能性，这种可能性源于一种信心：苏维埃公民在共产党的指导下，有能力通过意志将共产主义世界变为现实。这种期望与一种信念产生了共鸣：人类可以通过意志行为使整个宇宙按照其愿望的节奏运转。然而，与19世纪的浪漫主义意识形态相反，苏维埃共产党人坚持认为他们的意识形态是行动的意识形态。此外，他们知道自己的信仰植根于科学分析，这与浪漫主义的神秘主义取向形成鲜明对比。布哈林宣布：“在我们的条件下，浪漫主义与英雄主义有着特别的联系，它根本不指向形而上学的天空，而是指向大地及其方方面面，指向对敌人的胜利和对自然的胜利。”

Stalin’s toast bespoke limitless possibilities, stemming from the confidence that Soviet citizens, under the guidance of the Communist party, had the capacity to will the Communist world into existence. This expectation resonated with the belief that man could bend the whole universe to the rhythm of his desires by an act of will. In opposition to Romantic ideology of the nineteenth century, however, Soviet Communists insisted that theirs was an ideology of action. Furthermore, they knew their faith to be grounded in scientific analysis, in contrast to the mystical orientation of Romanticism. Bukharin declared: “In our conditions, the Romantic is connected in particular measure to the heroic, and it is not at all oriented to a metaphysical heaven, but instead to the earth, with all of its aspects, to victory over the enemy and to victory over nature.”
斯大林主义的新浪漫主义在另一个重要方面也不同于19世纪的浪漫主义精神。赋予苏维埃时代英雄的强大精神从未是绝对的或自发的；它是由共产党培育的，其表达能力归功于斯大林本人，他将自己描述为培养“每一个有能力和有理解力的工人”的“园丁，就像培育他心爱的果树一样”。
作为有表达能力的存在，苏维埃公民不再像富尔曼诺夫小说中的恰巴耶夫那样无意识且软弱如蜡——他们成长并开花，但生长在斯大林控制的园林景观中。斯大林培育果实累累的树木，修剪它们的茎干和枝条，并切除被认为对有序园林环境有害的部分。虽然这个园艺项目的历史进程要求对自我表达和个人成长进行更大的投入，但其首要着力点仍然是那些塑造、引导和干预个人生活的启蒙冲动。

Stalinist Neo-Romanticism differed from the nineteenth-century Romantic spirit in another significant respect. The powerful spirit ascribed to the heroes of the Soviet age was never absolute or self-in-duced; it was nurtured by the Communist party and owed its expressive power to Stalin himself, who described himself as rearing “every capable and understanding worker” like a “gardener, who rears his beloved fruit tree.”

As expressive beings Soviet citizens, unlike Chapaev in Furmanov’s novel, were no longer unconscious and soft like wax— they grew and blossomed, but in a garden landscape controlled by Stalin. Stalin fostered the fruit-carrying trees, he trimmed their stems and branches, and he excised parts deemed harmful for the ordered garden environment. While the historical progression of this gardening project mandated an ever greater investment in self-expression and individual growth, its primary emphasis remained on enlightened urges to shape, direct, and intervene in individuals’ lives.

如同对自我表达的号召一样，斯大林主义的镇压也具有个体化色彩。在发达的社会主义秩序中，个人不能再将不完美的社会环境视为其扭曲的根源；这是1920年代苏维埃法律所基于的假设。相比之下，斯大林时代的法律专家断言，“社会主义社会中对道德规范的背离，是资本主义残余在人的意识中的表现。”从现在起，个人要对自己的言行和思想负全部责任。正如一本流行的心理学教科书所言：“一个人参与了自己性格的塑造，他本人应对该性格负责。”个人的精神只能以两种方式之一出现——要么是善的，个人按照已经改变的环境塑造自己；要么是恶的，个人抗拒自我改造。因此，个人的意志要么表现为革命性和创造性的，要么表现为反革命性和破坏性的。当时的政治语言在赞颂斯达汉诺夫工作者超人的创造性努力的同时，也对意志的破坏力进行了残酷的描述，这种破坏力体现在“破坏分子”身上，其行为同样超出了人类的想象。“人民公敌”的邪恶意志如此之大，以至于必须将他们从苏维埃社会中清除。

Like the call to self-expression, Stalinist repression also had an individuating thrust. In a developed socialist order individuals could no longer point to an imperfect social environment as a source of their deformation; this had been the assumption on which Soviet law of the 1920s was built. By contrast, legal specialists of the Stalin era asserted that “divergences from the moral norm in a socialist society are the manifestations of the remnants of capitalism in the consciousness of man.” From now on, individuals were fully responsible for their deeds and thoughts. As a popular textbook on psychology stated: “A man takes part in the shaping of his own character and he himself bears a responsibility for that character.” The individual’s spirit could appear in only one of two ways—either as good, with the individual growing in the image of his transformed environment, or as evil, with the individual resisting his transformation. The individual’s will thus figured as either revolutionary and creative or counterrevolutionary and destructive. Even as it hailed the superhuman creative efforts of the Stakhanovites, the political language of the time engaged in grueling descriptions of the will’s destructive power, manifested in “wreckers,” whose actions were equally beyond human imagination. The evil will of the “enemies of the people” was such that they had to be removed from Soviet society.

党领导人对自己队伍中充斥着潜伏敌人的恐惧可以追溯到革命初期。但一旦苏维埃领导层决定构建乌托邦、废除阶级社会并着手建设社会主义，这种恐惧就变得更加强烈了。随着非苏维埃阶级的消失，环境失去了作为污染影响源的原始意义。从现在起，一切不纯洁现象都只能从个人灵魂中发出。以前通过阶级身份标记可识别的不纯洁，已经退缩到人类心理的深处。1930年代爆发的政治偏执，对所谓人民公敌怀疑的大规模增加，也表达了一种由于传统的马克思主义评价个人的阶级分析工具失效而引发的危机。当再没有异己阶级可供指认时，妖魔化通往社会主义道路上现有障碍的倾向变得势不可挡。

The fear among party leaders that their ranks were filled with hidden enemies dated back to the early revolutionary period. But this fear became much more acute once the Soviet leadership decided to construct utopia, to abolish class society and to proceed with the building of socialism. With the disappearance of non-Soviet classes, the environment lost its original significance as a polluting influence. From now on all instances of impurity could only emanate from individual souls. Impurity, previously discernible through the markers of class identification, had retracted into the depths of the human psyche. The exploding political paranoia of the 1930s, the massive increase in suspicion against supposed enemies of the people, also expressed a crisis induced by the breakdown of the traditional Marxist tool of class analysis in evaluating the individual. Where there were no more alien classes to point to, the proclivity to demonize existing obstacles on the road to socialism became overwhelming.

1930年代的大清洗是根据纯洁性对灵魂进行分类的巨大项目的顶点。在消灭所有被认为对新的社会主义秩序有害的个人时，恐怖是斯大林主义人道主义计划的另一面，该计划旨在创建一个以绝对纯洁精神定义的社会机体。同理，清洗是苏维埃国家另一种强有力的个体化技术，在此程度上，它促进了斯大林主义的主体化政策。在整个清洗期间，甚至在其最高峰，每天通过数千项判决时，被告都不是以简易方式受审，而是单独受审，国家机关依赖大量的起诉材料，而这些材料同样是以个人为单位组织的。国家在这个过程中投入的资源和精力——例如，在内务人民委员部（NKVD）讯问室配备全天候待命的秘书，负责打字和复印无数个人供词的一个又一个版本——如果仅被看作对任意性国家恐怖运动的掩饰，那将显得荒谬可笑。然而，如果将清洗看作是为了追求有关个人灵魂状态的无可辩驳的真相而构思的大规模分类项目，那么它就不那么荒谬了。
在整个清洗过程中，党领导人反复强调他们的个体化重点，尤其是调查中针对每个人所作的细致考察。莫斯科中心一再向“过度热心”的地方检察官发出训斥，指责他们以简易方式开除党员。“诚实的共产党员”被描述为受到了“不充分的个体研究”。以约瑟夫·斯大林为最高化身的党，将自己塑造成最终裁判，逐一审慎地权衡每个灵魂。

The Great Purges of the 1930s stood at the apex of an enormous project to classify souls according to purity. In exterminating all individuals deemed harmful to the new, socialist order, the terror was the flip side of the Stalinist humanist program of creating a social body defined in terms of absolute purity of spirit. By the same token, the purge was another powerful individualizing technique of the Soviet state, and to this extent it furthered the Stalinist policies of subjectivization. Throughout the purge period, even at its very height, when thousands of sentences were being passed daily, defendants were tried not in summary fashion, but individually, with the state organs relying on an enormous array of prosecutorial material, again organized by individuals. The amount of resources and effort that the state invested in this process—for instance, staffing NKVD interrogation cells with secretaries, available around the clock, who typed and copied version after version of countless individual confessions—cannot but appear grotesque if viewed as a mere cover-up for a campaign of arbitrary state terror. The purges appear less grotesque, though, when seen as a large-scale project of classification conceived for the pursuit of irrefutable truth regarding the state of individuals’ souls.

Throughout the purges, the party leaders repeatedly stressed their individualizing emphasis, specifically the degree of individual care they applied to the investigation. Time and again, the Moscow Center issued reprimands to “overzealous” local prosecutors whom it charged with expelling party members in summary fashion. “Honest Communists” were portrayed as receiving “insufficient individual study.” The party, embodied above all by Josef Stalin, cast itself as a final judge, weighing each soul individually and carefully.

zh: E. 克伦克尔（E. Krenkel’）著，《四战友日记》（Chetyre tovarishcha. Dnevnik）（莫斯科：北方海路总局出版社，1940年），第311页。斯大林在下令处决他的对手尼古拉·布哈林三天后，举行了这次为生命干杯的祝酒。
en:
E. Krenkel’, Chetyre tovarishcha. Dnevnik (Moscow: Izd. Glavsev-
morputi, 1940), 311. Stalin made this toast to life three days after di-
recting the execution of his rival Nikolai Bukharin.

zh: 《第一次全苏作家代表大会速记报告》，第501页。另见伦纳德·P. 韦塞尔（Leonard P. Wessell Jr.）著，《卡尔·马克思、浪漫主义讽刺与无产阶级：马克思主义的神话起源》（Karl Marx, Romantic Irony, and the Proletariat: The Mythopoetic Origins of Marxism）（巴吞鲁日：路易斯安那州立大学出版社，1979年）。
en:
Pervyi vsesoiuznyi s’’ezd sovetskikh pisatelei, 501. See also Leonard P.
Wessell Jr., Karl Marx, Romantic Irony, and the Proletariat: The Mytho-
poetic Origins of Marxism (Baton Rouge: Louisiana State University
Press, 1979).

zh: 《真理报》，1935年1月29日，第1–5版。斯大林的隐喻让人想起齐格蒙特·鲍曼（Zygmunt Bauman）关于极权政府即“园艺”的观念；见鲍曼著，《现代性与大屠杀》（Modernity and the Holocaust）（伊萨卡：康奈尔大学出版社，1989年）。
en:
Pravda, 1/29/1935, 1–5. Stalin’s metaphor brings to mind Zygmunt
Bauman’s notion of totalitarian government as “gardening”; Bau-
man, Modernity and the Holocaust (Ithaca: Cornell University Press,
1989).

zh: 引自雷蒙德·鲍尔（Raymond Bauer）著，《苏联心理学中的新人》（The New Man in Soviet Psychology）（马萨诸塞州剑桥：哈佛大学出版社，1952年），第147、149页。鲍里斯·格罗伊斯（Boris Groys）著，《斯大林主义的总体艺术：先锋派、审美独裁及其超越》（The Total Art of Stalinism: Avant-Garde, Aesthetic Dictatorship, and Beyond）（普林斯顿：普林斯顿大学出版社，1992年），第61页；哈尔芬著，《我灵魂中的恐怖》，第256–262页。
en:
Citations from Raymond Bauer, The New Man in Soviet Psychology
(Cambridge, Mass.: Harvard University Press, 1952), 147, 149. Boris
Grois, The Total Art of Stalinism: Avant-Garde, Aesthetic Dictatorship, and
Beyond (Princeton: Princeton University Press, 1992), 61; Halfin, Terror
in My Soul, 256–262.

zh: 鲍尔著，《苏联心理学中的新人》，第47页。哈尔芬著，《我灵魂中的恐怖》，第33–38页。当指代一个人信仰的核心时，20世纪30年代的布尔什维克经常使用“灵魂”一词。灵魂是个人性格和倾向的心理聚合。这种对人的本质主义理解与20世纪20年代的解释明显不同，后者将个人视为对社会和物理环境刺激作出反应的生理反射的复合体。
en:
Bauer, New Man in Soviet Psychology, 47. Halfin, Terror in My Soul, 33–38.
When referring to the core of a person’s convictions, Bolsheviks in
the 1930s frequently used the term “soul.” The soul was a psychologi-
cal aggregate of the person’s character and disposition. This essen-
tialist understanding of the person differed markedly from interpre-
tations of the 1920s, which viewed the individual as a composite of
physiological reflexes responding to stimuli in the social and physical
environment.

zh: 彼得·霍尔奎斯特著，《作为技术的国家暴力：苏联极权主义中的暴力逻辑》（“State Violence as Technique: The Logic of Violence in Soviet Totalitarianism”），载《美化人类花园：比较框架下的20世纪人口管理》（Landscaping the Human Garden: Twentieth-Century Population Management in a Comparative Framework），阿米尔·维纳（Amir Weiner）编（斯坦福：斯坦福大学出版社，2003年）。
en:
Peter Holquist, “State Violence as Technique: The Logic of Violence in
Soviet Totalitarianism,” in Landscaping the Human Garden: Twentieth-
Century Population Management in a Comparative Framework, ed. Amir
Weiner (Stanford: Stanford University Press, 2003).
